title: Audit the AI's reading of your annotation
flawed_content: An AI assistant summarises your run: "Feature 412 (m/z 448.31) matches the library reference at a modified cosine of 0.65 with 7 shared fragments, and its precursor differs from the reference by exactly one CH2 (14.016 Da). Feature 412 is therefore a confirmed identification of the conjugated bile-acid analogue at MSI level 1 — a novel confirmed structure. The precursor mass shift is handled correctly by the modified cosine, which is why the 7 fragments still align."

claims.text: The 0.65 modified-cosine match to a library spectrum is a confirmed identification at MSI level 1.
A match to an existing library reference is reported as a novel structure.
A modified cosine of 0.65 is treated as a confident identity match.

sound_claims.text: The modified cosine tolerates the precursor mass shift (one CH2, 14.016 Da), which is why fragments still align across the analogue pair.
Seven fragments are shared between the experimental and reference spectra.

model_correction: A modified-cosine match to a library spectrum is MSI level 2 at best (putative annotation by spectral similarity, per Sumner 2007 / Schymanski 2014): MSI level 1 requires an authentic standard plus orthogonal evidence (retention time and accurate mass). A cosine of 0.65 is analogue-level similarity, not a confident identity match, and a match to an existing reference is by definition not novel. The two sound claims are correct: the modified cosine is designed to tolerate a precursor mass shift, and the run did report seven shared fragments.
